questions.q:
Assertion(A): The maximum covalency of Si and Ge is 6 but that of carbon is 4.
Reason (R): Due to the presence of d-orbitals in Si and Ge, both these elements can undergo $\mathrm{sp}^3 \mathrm{~d}^2$ hybridisation and covalency of 6 is possible. Carbon has no d-orbitals in it and hence its covalency is 4.
The correct answer is:
options: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
(A) and (R) are correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
(A) is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): The maximum covalency of Si and Ge is 6, but that of carbon is 4. This is a correct statement. Carbon can form four bonds, achieving a maximum covalency of 4. However, silicon and germanium, being in the same group but a period below carbon, can expand their valence shell to accommodate more than 8 electrons, allowing them to form up to six covalent bonds.
- Reason (R): Due to the presence of d-orbitals in Si and Ge, both these elements can undergo \(\mathrm{sp}^3 d^2\) hybridisation and a covalency of 6 is possible. Carbon has no \(d\)-orbitals in it and hence its covalency is 4. This is a correct explanation. The key difference between carbon and the heavier elements in its group is the availability of empty \(\mathrm{d}\)-orbitals. These \(\mathrm{d}\)-orbitals allow silicon and germanium to undergo hybridization beyond \(\mathrm{sp}^3\) to form molecules like \(\mathrm{SiF}_6^{2-}\) or \(\mathrm{GeCl}_6^{2-}\), in which the central atom has a coordination number of 6. Carbon lacks these dorbitals, which limits its covalency to 4.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following
a) Borax gives blue coloured $\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}_2\right)_2$ when heated with $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ salt.
b) The correct formula of Borax is $\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{~B}_4 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{OH})_4\right] 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
c) Trihalides of boron are Lewis bases.
questions.solution:
- a) Borax gives blue colored \(\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}_2\right)_2\) when heated with \(\mathrm{Co}^{2+}\) salt. This is correct. This is a classic test for metal ions using the borax bead test. When borax is heated, it forms a glassy bead of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride. In the presence of a cobalt salt, cobalt metaborate, \(\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{BO}_2\right)_2\), is formed, which gives a characteristic blue color.
- b) The correct formula of Borax is \(\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{~B}_4 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{OH})_4\right] \cdot 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\). This is correct. This is the more accurate formula for borax (sodium tetraborate decahydrate), highlighting the presence of a tetraborate anion with a specific structure.
- c) Trihalides of boron are Lewis bases. This is incorrect. Boron trihalides (\(B X_3\)) are Lewis acids because boron has an incomplete octet in these compounds and can accept a pair of electrons.
Statements \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) are correct.

b) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 / \mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$buffer system helps to maintain $\mathrm{pH}$ of blood between 7.26 and 7.42
c) Graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperatures
questions.solution:
- a) \(C_{60}\) molecule has 12 six-membered rings and 20 five-membered rings. This is incorrect. The \(C_{60}\) fullerene molecule, also known as buckminsterfullerene, has a spherical structure with 12 five-membered rings and 20 six-membered rings.
- b) \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 / \mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}\) buffer system helps to maintain pH of blood between 7.26 and 7.42. This is correct. The carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system is a crucial component of blood plasma that resists changes in pH, keeping it within a narrow range required for proper physiological function.
- c) Graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperatures. This is correct. Graphite consists of layers that can slide over one another easily, giving it lubricating properties. It is particularly effective at high temperatures where conventional liquid lubricants would vaporize.
Statements \(\mathrm{b}\) and \(\mathrm{c}\) are correct.

Identify correct statements from the following:
i. \(\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3\) is a monobasic acid.
ii. The correct formula of borax is \(\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{~B}_4 \mathrm{O}_5(\mathrm{OH})_3\right] 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\).
iii. \(\mathrm{NaBH}_4\) is a reducing agent.
questions.solution:
The explanations of given statements are as follows : (i) \(\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{BO}_3\) is a monobasic acid because in aqueous solution, it coordinates with a molecule of water to form a hydrated species,
\(\mathrm{B}^{3+}\) ion pulls the \(\sigma\)-electron charge of coordinated \(\mathrm{O}\)-atom towards itself. The coordinated oxygen, in turn, pull the \(\sigma\)-electrons of \(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond of the attached water molecule towards itself. This facilitates the removal of \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\)ion from the \(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond. It can be written as follows: \(\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_4 \Gamma+\mathrm{H}^{+}\right.\) (ii) The correct formula for borax is \(\mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{~B}_4 \mathrm{O}_7\right] \cdot 10 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\). (iii) \(\mathrm{NaBH}_4\) is a selective reducing agent for aldehydes, ketones and ester. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) are correct.

Thus, statements (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are correct.

II. Boron does not show +1 as stable oxidation state. As we move down this group stability of +1 oxidation state increase. But +1 oxidation state of B is least stable.

III. Maximum covalency of Boron is four, since it can not have more than eight electrons in its outmost orbit.

IV. Boron does not form BF66- ion, since it can not have more than eight electrons in its outmost orbit.

(b) In BCl3·NH3, boron has tetrahedral geometry. 

(c) Aqueous solution of borax is acidic.
questions.solution:
1. In orthoboric acid H3BO3, boron is sp2 hybridized and thus is in planar geometry.

2. In BCl3.NH3, Boron and Nitrogen (N)are both sp3 hybridized and the shape of the adduct is tetrahedral .

3. Combination of a strong base and a weak acid results in a salt which is basic in nature. Borax is a salt which is formed by the reaction of NaOH (strong base) with H3BO3 (weak acid). Thus, the aqueous solution of borax is basic and not acidic.

Which of the following statements is/are correct for group 13 elements?
A. Al reacts with dil. $\mathrm{HCl}$ to liberate $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas
B. Al reacts with conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ to liberate $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas
C. Boron reacts with only acids to liberate $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas
D. Anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ reacts with moisture to liberate $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas
questions.solution:
A. When $\mathrm{Al}$ reacts with dil. $\mathrm{HCl}$, it liberates $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas.
$2 \mathrm{Al}+6 \mathrm{HCl}\left(\text { dil.) } \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{AlCl}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2\right.$
B. When Al reacts with conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ than it liberates NO gas.
$\mathrm{Al}+4 \mathrm{HNO}_3 \text { (conc.) } \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_3+\mathrm{NO}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
C. Crystalline boron does not react with boiling $\mathrm{HCl}, \mathrm{HF}, \mathrm{HI}$ etc.
D. $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ reacts with moisture and form aluminium hydroxide.
$\mathrm{AlCl}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_3+3 \mathrm{HCl}$
Hence, option (4) is correct.

III. $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ is soluble in conc. $\mathrm{NaOH}$.
questions.solution:
(I) Catenation property of group 14 elements decreases from carbon to tin. Carbon is small atom, thus the bond formed between two carbon atom is strong. Therefore, it shows maximum catenation. As we move down the group, size of atom increases, so $M-M$ bond strength decreases and tendency to show catenation decreases. Thus, lead does not show catenation property.
(II) Fullerene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{60}\right)$ has 20 six-membered carbon rings and 12 five-membered carbon rings.
(III) $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ is soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH}$ or alkaline solution. $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ is an acidic oxide.
$2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SiO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

Thus, option (2) is correct.
